teachingQuestion: Which information-flow rule protects the stated property?
focalInsight: Confidentiality and integrity models use opposite-looking read/write constraints because they protect different harms.
title: Security models: protected property before rule
caption: Read the protected objective first; then apply the corresponding flow or transaction rule.

nodes.label: Bell-LaPadula
nodes.detail: Confidentiality: no read up, no write down

nodes.label: Biba
nodes.detail: Integrity: no read down, no write up

nodes.label: Clark-Wilson
nodes.detail: Integrity: well-formed transactions and separation of duties

altSummary: A four-row comparison lists Bell-LaPadula, Biba, Clark-Wilson, and Brewer-Nash with the property or conflict each addresses.
textFallback: Bell-LaPadula protects confidentiality through information-flow restrictions such as no read up and no write down. Biba protects integrity through no read down and no write up. Clark-Wilson protects integrity through controlled transactions and separation of duties. Brewer-Nash limits access that would create a conflict after access to a competitor’s information.
